lines.text: At 1:23 in the morning, a nuclear reactor in Soviet Ukraine... was destroyed.
lines.tts: At one twenty-three in the morning, a nuclear reactor in Soviet Ukraine... was destroyed.

lines.text: A few kilometres away, tens of thousands of people lived ordinary lives in the city of Pripyat.
lines.tts: A few kilometres away, tens of thousands of people lived ordinary lives, in the city of Pripyat.

lines.text: That night, during a safety test on Reactor 4, a flawed design and operating errors combined... and the power surged.
lines.tts: That night, during a safety test on Reactor Four, a flawed design and operating errors combined... and the power surged.

lines.text: Two explosions tore the reactor open. The fire released radioactive material into the air.
lines.tts: Two explosions tore the reactor open. The fire released radioactive material into the air.

lines.text: Firefighters and plant workers rushed in, facing an emergency whose full scale was not yet understood.
lines.tts: Firefighters and plant workers rushed in, facing an emergency whose full scale, was not yet understood.

lines.text: That Saturday, life in Pripyat carried on. Many residents had little idea of the danger nearby.
lines.tts: That Saturday, life in Pripyat carried on. Many residents had little idea, of the danger nearby.

lines.text: About thirty-six hours after the explosion, the buses came. Residents were told the evacuation was temporary.
lines.tts: About thirty-six hours after the explosion, the buses came. Residents were told, the evacuation was temporary.

lines.text: They never came back. In 1986 alone, about 116,000 people were evacuated.
lines.tts: They never came back. In nineteen eighty-six alone, about one hundred and sixteen thousand people were evacuated.

lines.text: Its consequences are still felt today, and it changed how the world sees nuclear safety.
lines.tts: Its consequences are still felt today... and it changed how the world sees nuclear safety.
